source_policy: Canonical terms and definitions are authored by Bloomery contributors or reference public standard identifiers only. Restricted standards text is never redistributed.

disambiguation_rules.resolution: Shared by phosphorus and sulfur in steelmaking context; resolve from the surrounding composition element being discussed, and keep both when the context is residual-element control in general.

terms.definition: Chinese carbon structural steel grade with nominal yield strength 235 MPa and quality level B. Property values require product form, thickness, and applicable standard context.
Chinese high-strength low-alloy structural steel grade with nominal yield strength 355 MPa and quality level B. Property values require thickness, temperature, and standard context.
Chinese high-strength low-alloy structural steel grade with nominal yield strength 460 MPa and quality level C, including 0-degree-C impact requirements.
Chinese quality carbon structural steel with nominal carbon content around 0.45 percent by mass. Heat-treatment response depends on section size and cooling rate.
Primary strengthening element in steel; governs strength, hardness, and weldability trade-offs.
Deoxidizer and solid-solution strengthening element commonly reported in heat composition.
Strengthening element that combines with sulfur to reduce hot shortness risk.
Residual element that increases cold brittleness; limited by grade specifications.
Residual element that promotes hot shortness and manganese-sulfide inclusions; limited by grade specifications.
Stress at which a material begins to deform plastically; measured per the applicable tensile test standard.
Maximum engineering stress sustained during a tensile test before necking or fracture.
Percentage increase of the gauge length after fracture in a tensile test.
Energy absorbed by a Charpy V-notch specimen at a specified test temperature.
Resistance to localized indentation; the numeric value is only comparable within the same hardness scale.
Composition-derived index estimating hardenability and cold-crack sensitivity; the numeric value depends on the formula version, so formula identity must always be recorded.
Local separation of material that may originate during casting, rolling, heat treatment, or welding.
Cavity formed by trapped gas during solidification.
Non-metallic particle such as oxide or sulfide retained in the steel matrix; severity is rated per the applicable standard.
Local enrichment of solute elements caused by uneven solidification.
Chinese national standard for carbon structural steels. Referenced by identifier only; the standard text is not redistributed.

terms.definition: International standard for metallic tensile testing at room temperature. Referenced by identifier only; the standard text is not redistributed.
Primary steelmaking stage that converts hot metal into crude steel by oxygen blowing.
Secondary metallurgy stage for temperature, composition, inclusion, and cleanliness control before casting.
Vacuum circulation refining stage for decarburization and hydrogen, nitrogen, and oxygen removal.
Process that solidifies molten steel into a semi-finished strand such as slab, bloom, or billet.
Stage that reheats cast strands to the rolling temperature window before hot rolling.
Deformation stage above the recrystallization temperature that sets final dimensions and microstructure.
Stable identifier for a traceable melt or heat in production data.
Rectangular semi-finished casting that is the typical feed of hot strip mills.
